property_summary: For any fuzzed address a, calling transferOwnership(a) as the current owner must set owner to exactly a (owner == newOwner); the mutant instead sets owner to msg.sender, breaking this for any a != msg.sender.
For any newOwner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) as the current owner must set c.owner() to newOwner; the mutant never updates owner, so it stays address(0).

For any address newOwner and the current owner (address(0)), a call to transferOwnership must set owner to exactly newOwner — including address(0); the mutant wrongly reverts for newOwner == address(0), leaving owner unchanged.
For every caller, calling `owned()` must revert unless the caller is the current owner; the mutant removes this check so any non-owner's call succeeds, breaking the rule.

Only the owner may change ownership: for any non-owner caller and any newOwner, transferOwnership must revert and leave owner unchanged; the mutant drops the guard, so a non-owner's call succeeds and owner changes, breaking the invariant.

Once the current owner sets ownership to a chosen address, a subsequent transferOwnership call from any other caller must be rejected, leaving the owner at that chosen address; the guard-dropping mutant lets the second caller overwrite the owner.

Since C's owner starts at address(0), for every admissible caller that is not address(0) and every proposed newOwner, transferOwnership must revert and leave owner() at address(0); the mutant drops the guard so such a call succeeds and changes owner(), violating the rule.
Only the current owner may successfully call transferOwnership (any other caller must revert); the mutant inverts the modifier so non-owners succeed and the owner is rejected.

property_summary: For any address actor, after ownership is transferred to actor, calling owned() from actor must succeed (onlyOwner grants access to the current owner); the mutant's != check makes the owner's own call revert.

For any caller equal to the current owner and any newOwner, a successful transferOwnership must set owner() to newOwner; the mutant reverts on every call so owner() never changes and the rule fails for some fuzzed newOwner.
After any successful transferOwnership(new), c.owner() must equal the passed argument; the mutant instead sets owner to address(0), breaking this for any nonzero argument.
For any non-owner caller, invoking owned() must revert; the mutant removed onlyOwner so a non-owner call succeeds, breaking the access-control invariant.

After ownership is set to a nonzero address, transferOwnership succeeds if and only if the caller equals c.owner(); the buggy modifier (msg.sender == address(0)) instead rejects the rightful owner, so the rule fails for the fuzzed caller equal to the owner.

For any caller that is not the current owner (initial owner is address(0)), calling transferOwnership must leave the owner unchanged; the buggy modifier with the deleted require lets any caller change it.
For any non-owner caller, calling transferOwnership always reverts and leaves the owner unchanged; the mutant (require deleted) lets any caller succeed and change the owner.

For any caller equal to c.owner(), owned() must complete without reverting (the function body runs after the onlyOwner check); the mutant always reverts, so it fails for the caller whose address equals owner.

property_summary: For any fuzzed actor that the owner has transferred ownership to, calling owned() as that actor must complete without reverting; the mutant's owned() always reverts, so it breaks this for the new owner.

For any caller, calling owned() must never change the stored owner (it remains address(0) since owner was never transferred); the buggy version overwrites owner with msg.sender, so owner() differs after the call.

For any non-zero caller, calling owned() must not confer ownership: a subsequent transferOwnership by that same caller must still revert (since ownership was never granted); the mutant makes owned() set owner = msg.sender, so the follow-up transfer succeeds.

After ownership is transferred to a fuzzed actor, a subsequent owned() call by the initial owner (address(0)) must leave owner() unchanged; the mutant makes owned() overwrite owner with msg.sender (address(0)), destroying the transferred ownership.

For any caller, calling owned() must never change the stored owner: it either reverts or leaves owner() exactly as it was before the call; the mutant overwrites owner with the caller, so for the caller equal to the current owner (address(0)) it completes and observably rewrites owner(), breaking the rule.

For any caller that is not the current owner, owned() must revert without changing anything; the mutant lets any non-zero caller execute it and silently grant themselves ownership, so the call succeeds where the reference reverts.
